Goal: Restore/compose personal messages to friends — recreate the content of messages that were lost or want to be re-sent — while keeping the writing natural and not referencing any AI assistance.

Reusable process template
1. Gather context
   - Who is the friend? (name, relationship, shared experiences)
   - Purpose of message: apology, catching up, event invite, update, etc.
   - Tone: formal, casual, humorous, supportive.
   - Key facts to include: dates, decisions, mutual friends, relevant details.

2. Draft core points
   - Open with a personal greeting that fits the relationship.
   - Mention the reason for reaching out and any necessary context.
   - Recreate specifics you remember (events, emotions, plans).
   - Close with a friendly sign-off and next steps or invitation.

3. Edit for naturalness and privacy
   - Use the friend’s name and personal references.
   - Avoid mentioning how the message was generated.
   - Keep sentences concise and warm.

Examples — several message types

1) Friendly catch-up (casual)
Hi Alex — I realized we haven't caught up in ages. How have you been? I still think about that hiking trip we talked about last summer; if you're free next month I'd love to finally make it happen. Work has been hectic but I'm carving out more weekends for friends. Want to grab coffee the weekend of the 12th? Let me know what works for you. — Sam

2) Apology and restoration of a lost message
Hey Maria — I’m sorry if my last message got lost; I wanted to say I really appreciated you helping me move last weekend. I know I didn’t say it properly at the time, but it meant a lot. I owe you dinner — when are you free next week so I can take you out? Thanks again for being such a great friend. — Leo

3) Making plans (specific details)
Hi Priya — Quick note to confirm our plans: dinner at Luna Bistro on Friday at 7 pm. I booked a table under my name for four. If that doesn't work, we can push to Saturday evening. I’ll bring the extra charger and the playlist we talked about. See you Friday! — Jordan

4) Supportive message (sensitive topic)
Hey Samira — I heard about the interview and wanted to say I'm rooting for you. You've prepared so well and your track record speaks for itself. If you want to run through potential questions or need someone to review your presentation, I’m happy to help. No pressure either way — just know I’m here. — Nina

5) Short check-in (concise)
Morning Ben — Just checking in on how the project presentation went. Hope it went smoothly! Want to celebrate this weekend if you’re free. — Riley

Reproducible code-like template (for programmatic generation of messages)
- inputs:
  - name (string)
  - relationship (string; e.g., friend, colleague)
  - purpose (string; e.g., catch-up, apology, invite, support)

- name = "Eli"
- relationship = "friend"
- purpose = "invite"
- tone = "casual"

Notes and best practices
- Personalize each message to the recipient — include small shared details to make the message feel genuine.
- Keep the tone consistent with your relationship.
- If reconstructing a lost message, focus on the essentials (purpose, specifics, feelings) so the recipient gets the intended meaning even if the original phrasing is different.
